Vowels can be short or long. A long vowel says its name. A short vowel does not.

header.text: The letter o is a vowel. When o is followed by just consonants, o does not say its name. It makes a short o sound (/ŏ/).
When o is followed by a consonant and a silent e, o says its name. It makes a long o sound (/ō/).
When o is followed by another vowel, the two vowels can make a vowel team. In vowel teams that start with o, o says its name. It makes a long o sound. The other vowel is silent.

Toad's Sore Throat

textContent.text: Toad taps his throat. "Oh no! I can't croak!" He looks at the clock. "The big show is close. I need my croak to tell my jokes!"
Toad hops up the road to Mole's home.
"Mole! Help!" he calls. "I can't croak! No joke!"
Mole nods and runs to the stove. He puts hot oats into a bowl.
"Blow, then eat," Mole says. "Now try to croak."
Toad lets out a low, slow croak.
Mole grins. "You're set. Go win that show!"

Crow flaps his wings. "Now I know who grows the best plants—Goat!"

header.text: Put the sentences in order. The verb in each sentence can help you.

sentences.text: The girl pulled the wagon outside.
The verb pulled ends in -ed. It tells about something that has already happened. It tells about the past.
The girl pulls the wagon up the hill.
The verb pulls ends with -s. It tells about something that is happening now. It tells about the present.
The girl will pull the wagon down the road.
The verb will pull has the word will. It tells about something that is going to happen. It tells about the future.
